title: [Enhancement/UI]: Game Modal Elapsed Session Timer Pill in Toolbar Header
body:
## Problem
Once a player launches a game inside the modal, there is no lightweight timer visible in the modal toolbar showing how long the current play session has been running without exiting to external clocks.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/modal-session-timer.css`:
   - Compact monospace pill (`MM:SS` / `HH:MM:SS`) positioned cleanly inside the game modal header alongside existing controls, with subtle paused state indicator.
2. Create modular controller `assets/js/modal-session-timer.js`:
   - Implement `ModalSessionTimer` with `start()`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `reset()`, and `formatElapsed(ms)`.
   - Automatically pause accumulation when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` and clean up `setInterval` cleanly on modal close.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/CSS3, zero external libraries, zero Unicode emojis.
4. Add standalone unit test `scripts/test-modal-session-timer.js` using Node's `node:test` and `assert` verifying time formatting (`00:00`, `05:42`, `1:02:09`), visibility pause logic, and reset cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Elapsed session timer starts cleanly on modal launch and formats `MM:SS` accurately.
- [ ] Timer pauses automatically when switching browser tabs and resumes cleanly on return.
- [ ] Closing the modal resets and clears active intervals with zero memory leaks.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-modal-session-timer.js` passes cleanly under `node`.
- [ ] Protected core files (`index.html`, `leaderboard.html`, `games-registry.js`) remain untouched.

title: [Enhancement/UX]: Undo Toast Guard for Destructive Favorites and History Clears

2. Create modular utility `assets/js/undo-toast-guard.js`:
   - Implement `UndoToastGuard.scheduleAction({ label, snapshot, onCommit, onUndo, durationMs = 5000 })`.
   - Defer irreversible storage wipe or restore deep-cloned snapshot immediately if `"Undo"` is clicked before timer expiry; flush pending commits safely on page unload.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/CSS3, zero dependencies, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-undo-toast-guard.js` validating timer-based commit, immediate undo rollback, and overlapping action flush behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Countdown bar animates smoothly and auto-commits when expired.
- [ ] Triggering a second destructive action flushes the previous pending commit safely without losing either action.

title: [Enhancement/Audio]: Web Audio Suspended State Auto-Resume Banner Prompt
body:
## Problem
Modern browsers block Web Audio `AudioContext` playback until a direct user gesture occurs, causing newly loaded audio synthesizers or ambient soundscapes to silently fail if `context.state === 'suspended'`.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/audio-resume-banner.css`:
   - Subtle, dismissible floating audio prompt banner (`"Audio is muted by browser policy - Tap anywhere or click Enable Sound"`).
2. Create modular helper `assets/js/audio-resume-banner.js`:
   - Monitor registered `AudioContext` instances; display prompt only when audio features are enabled yet `ctx.state === 'suspended'`.
   - Attach one-time `pointerdown`/`keydown` unlock listeners that call `ctx.resume()` and hide the banner smoothly once `state === 'running'`.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Web Audio API, zero external packages, zero emojis.
4. Add automated test `scripts/test-audio-resume-banner.js` verifying suspended-state detection, resume promise resolution, and listener cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Banner appears only when Web Audio is suspended by autoplay rules while sound is enabled.
- [ ] Clicking Enable Sound or interacting unlocks `AudioContext` and dismisses the banner.
- [ ] Cleanly handles environments without `AudioContext` support.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-audio-resume-banner.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Enhancement/A11y]: Visual Tab-Order Sequence Overlay Helper for Focus Audits

   - Provide `enableAudit()`, `disableAudit()`, and `toggleAudit()` API removing all injected overlay nodes cleanly on disable.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/CSS3, zero external packages, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-tab-order-audit.js` verifying focusable selector filtering, positive `tabindex` ordering rules, and complete DOM cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Toggling Tab-Order Audit overlays sequential numeric badges across all visible keyboard-focusable controls.
- [ ] Positive `tabindex` ordering and disabled element exclusion follow W3C HTML spec rules.
- [ ] Disabling audit removes 100% of overlay badges with zero leftover DOM nodes.

body:
## Problem
Early 1980s IBM PC games pioneered the unmistakable high-contrast 4-color CGA (Color Graphics Adapter) look—specifically Palette 1 (Pitch Black, Glowing Cyan, Electric Magenta, Crisp White) and Palette 0 (Black, Green, Red, Brown)—which is not yet represented in ArcadeVerse's theme lineup.

4. Add unit test `scripts/test-newtons-cradle.js` verifying exact elastic equal-mass velocity swap, momentum conservation $\sum m_i v_i$, and sub-unity restitution energy decay.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pulling and releasing 1, 2, or 3 pendulum spheres cleanly transfers impulses across the resting chain.
- [ ] Variable mass and restitution sliders noticeably alter bounce and momentum transfer physics.
- [ ] High-restitution swings stay stable without runaway energy gain or ball overlap.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-newtons-cradle.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Graphics]: Procedural Hilbert, Peano and Gosper Space-Filling Curve Animator
body:
## Problem
Space-filling fractal curves (Hilbert, Peano, and Gosper flowsnake) continuously map a 1D line across every cell of a 2D grid without ever crossing themselves, creating an iconic algorithmic animation missing from ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/space-filling-curves.css`:
   - Canvas viewport with controls for Curve Family (`Hilbert`, `Peano`, `Moore`, `Gosper Flowsnake`), Recursion Order (`1`–`6` safely capped per family), Drawing Speed, Color Mode (`Progress Rainbow`, `Neon Cyan`, `Phosphor Green`), and Play/Pause/Replay buttons.
2. Create modular curve generator `assets/js/space-filling-curves.js`:
   - Generate exact ordered 2D point arrays `[ {x, y}, ... ]` via recursive/iterative index-to-XY algorithms (e.g. Hilbert bit-manipulation `d2xy` or deterministic recursive generators) with strict vertex count bounds preventing memory stalls.
   - Animate progressive polyline drawing along normalized path length with smooth gradient coloring.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas, zero external dependencies, zero emojis.
4. Add automated test `scripts/test-space-filling-curves.js` validating exact vertex counts (`4^n` for Hilbert order `n`, `9^n` for Peano), unit-step adjacency between consecutive points, and zero self-intersections.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hilbert, Peano, Moore, and Gosper curves animate smoothly along their full continuous paths.
- [ ] Recursion order caps safely prevent browser freezes on deep orders.
- [ ] Color gradient traces progress cleanly from start vertex to end vertex.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-space-filling-curves.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected core files remain untouched.

title: [Feature/Audio]: Interactive Web Audio Shepard Tone & Perpetual Pitch Illusion Synthesizer
body:
## Problem
The Shepard Tone (and Risset Glissando) is a famous auditory illusion used in arcade tension loops and cinema where overlapping octave-spaced sine partials appear to rise or descend endlessly in pitch forever, an audio phenomenon not yet built in ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. Create isolated stylesheet `assets/css/shepard-tone.css`:
   - Laboratory interface with Direction toggle (`Ascending`, `Descending`, `Paused`), Sweep Speed slider, Octave Voice Count (`4`–`10`), Base Center Frequency slider, Master Volume, and a live spectral bell-curve + gliding partial canvas visualizer.
2. Create modular audio illusion engine `assets/js/shepard-tone.js`:
   - Drive `N` continuous `OscillatorNode` partials spaced cleanly in log-frequency octaves (`f_i = f_min * 2^(phase_i * span)`), wrapping seamlessly at octave boundaries.
   - Weight each oscillator's `GainNode` by a smooth Gaussian bell envelope centered in log-frequency space so boundary wrap-arounds happen at near-zero amplitude with zero audible clicks.
   - Render real-time Gaussian bell envelope and moving octave dots on a 2D Canvas synced to audio phase.
3. Pure Vanilla JS/Web Audio API/Canvas, zero external libraries, zero emojis.
4. Add unit test `scripts/test-shepard-tone.js` validating Gaussian bell gain symmetry, seamless phase wrap-around `[0, 1)`, and total RMS/gain normalization bounds preventing clipping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Overlapping octave partials create a convincing continuous endless ascending or descending pitch illusion without boundary clicks.
- [ ] Live spectral bell canvas accurately tracks every active partial's frequency and gain amplitude.
- [ ] Audio cleanly pauses, reverses direction, and cleans up oscillator nodes on stop/close.
- [ ] Standalone test `scripts/test-shepard-tone.js` passes under `node`.
- [ ] Protected files remain untouched.
